bill.title: Accelerating Access to Critical Therapies for ALS Reauthorization Act of 2026
bill.latestActionText: Received in the Senate. Read twice. Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 466.
subjects: Department of Health and Human Services
bill.officialSummary: Accelerating Access to Critical Therapies for ALS Reauthorization Act of 2026 This bill reauthorizes through FY2031 and revises programs that support research and development of drugs and other therapies to address amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (also known as ALS or Lou Gehrig's disease) and other neurodegenerative diseases. The bill reauthorizes grants from the National Institutes of Health (NIH) for scientific research on investigational drugs to prevent or treat ALS for individuals not otherwise eligible for clinical trials, grants from the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for research and development of therapies to prevent and treat ALS and other neurodegenerative diseases, and a Public-Private Partnership including the FDA and NIH that supports development and regulatory review of treatments for neurodegenerative diseases. Also, the NIH, in considering renewal of its grants, must assess available information on the safety and efficacy of the investigational drugs. It must also require grantees to promptly report serious and unexpected adverse events associated with their investigational drugs. Additionally, the FDA must publish a plan describing actions it will take over a five-year period to foster development of safe and effective drugs, and facilitate access to investigational drugs, that treat ALS and other rare neurodegenerative diseases. The FDA must also publish a report describing the actions it has taken under the plan.

classification.plainSummary: This bill extends funding through fiscal year 2031 for federal programs that support research and development of treatments for ALS (Lou Gehrig's disease) and similar neurodegenerative diseases. It requires the National Institutes of Health to track safety data on experimental drugs and mandates that the Food and Drug Administration publish a five-year plan describing how it will help develop and approve therapies for these rare diseases. The bill also continues a public-private partnership between federal agencies and outside organizations working on neurodegenerative disease treatments.

industries.rationale: The bill directly funds research grants and regulatory pathways for development of drugs and therapies targeting ALS and neurodegenerative diseases.
Providers treating ALS patients may see changes in available investigational therapies and clinical trial access, though the bill focuses primarily on research and regulatory processes.

plain.whatItDoes: This bill would renew through the 2031 budget year and change programs that support research and development of drugs and other therapies to address amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (also known as ALS or Lou Gehrig's disease) and other neurodegenerative diseases.
plain.whoItTouches: People with an illness that is still being studied. Anyone who uses the internet.
plain.everydayEffect: If it passed, the change would show up in what research gets funded. Nothing has changed yet. Most bills never become law.
plain.source: Reworded from the official summary. Staff at the Congressional Research Service wrote that summary. It is public domain, and the full text of it is further down this page.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
